At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. We welcome everyone who wants to belong and grow in a diverse and passionate culture, coupled with an attractive compensation and benefits package. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to knowledge How can you make a difference? The Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) is an international household survey programme developed and supported by UNICEF, designed to collect estimates of key indicators used to assess the situation of children and women. Over the past 30 years, Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) has expanded from 28 indicators in the first round to more than 200 indicators in the current seventh round (MICS 7), becoming one of the leading global sources of internationally comparable data on children and women, including child protection, early childhood development and education, child health and nutrition. In Uzbekistan, UNICEF Country Office has supported the last MICS survey in 2021-2022 and initiated support to MICS-7 in 2026 within the new Country Programme Document for 2026-2030. To ensure smooth implementation and to provide necessary assistance to National Statistics Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan (NSC), UNICEF Uzbekistan will hire a full-time consultant to oversee the MICS process from preparatory work to release of results. The MICS7 will be implemented using CAPI (Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing) to reduce data collection time, facilitate real-time monitoring, improve data quality and reduce survey costs. Under the overall supervision of the Monitoring and Evaluation (CRM) Specialist, the National MICS consultant will support the preparation, implementation and completion of the MICS survey in Uzbekistan. The consultant will work closely with and advise the NSC, especially the Survey Coordinator and sampling and data processing experts, during survey planning, questionnaire design, sampling, training, fieldwork, data processing, data analysis, dissemination and archiving, ensuring that MICS protocols and recommendations are followed at all times. The consultant will communicate effectively between the UNICEF CO and NSC, participate in required meetings, and coordinate the work of other resource people hired by UNICEF to provide technical assistance. The Consultant will work in close collaboration with the Regional MICS Coordinators at UNICEF Regional Office and the MICS Team at UNICEF Headquarters, as well as expert consultants assigned to support the Uzbekistan MICS (collectively labelled "The UNICEF MICS Team"). If you would like to know more about this consultancy, please review the complete Terms of Reference here: TMC0006563 External ToR .pdf To qualify as an advocate for every child you will have... Education: Master's degree in Social Sciences, Statistics, Demography, Epidemiology or any other related technical field Master's degree in Social Sciences, Statistics, Demography, Epidemiology or any other related technical field Proven minimum of 10 years’ experience in the coordination and/or management of quantitative household surveys (prior MICS or Demographic and Health Survey (DHS) experience requested); experience with CAPI data collection; training experience and ability to organize and facilitate training and presentations; experience in data analysis and survey report writing; strong computer skills and expertise in statistical analyses (familiarity with data processing and analysis software, particularly SPSS). Excellent oral and written communications in Uzbek, Russian and English required, knowledge of Karakalpak is an asset. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills; demonstrated ability to work in a multicultural environment and to establish harmonious and effective relationships both within and outside the organisation, specifically with National Statistical Offices; demonstrated leadership, managerial and supervisory ability; ability and willingness to travel extensively in Uzbekistan and attend regional workshops Desirables: Familiarity and previous experience of working with MICS in Uzbekistan is highly desirable. Familiarity and previous experience of working with MICS in Uzbekistan is highly desirable. For every Child, you demonstrate... At UNICEF, we are committed, passionate, and proud of what we do for as long as we are needed. Promoting the rights of every child is not just a job – it is a calling. UNICEF is a place where careers are built. We offer our staff diverse opportunities for professional and personal development that will help them reinforce a sense of purpose while serving children and communities across the world. Visit our website to learn more about what we do at UNICEF. For every child, the right to knowledge How can you make a difference? The Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) is an international household survey programme developed and supported by UNICEF, designed to collect estimates of key indicators used to assess the situation of children and women. Over the past 30 years, Multiple Indicator Cluster Surveys (MICS) has expanded from 28 indicators in the first round to more than 200 indicators in the current seventh round (MICS 7), becoming one of the leading global sources of internationally comparable data on children and women, including child protection, early childhood development and education, child health and nutrition. In Uzbekistan, UNICEF Country Office has supported the last MICS survey in 2021-2022 and initiated support to MICS-7 in 2026 within the new Country Programme Document for 2026-2030. To ensure smooth implementation and to provide necessary assistance to National Statistics Committee of the Republic of Uzbekistan (NSC), UNICEF Uzbekistan will hire a full-time consultant to oversee the MICS process from preparatory work to release of results. The MICS7 will be implemented using CAPI (Computer-Assisted Personal Interviewing) to reduce data collection time, facilitate real-time monitoring, improve data quality and reduce survey costs. Under the overall supervision of the Monitoring and Evaluation (CRM) Specialist, the National MICS consultant will support the preparation, implementation and completion of the MICS survey in Uzbekistan. The consultant will work closely with and advise the NSC, especially the Survey Coordinator and sampling and data processing experts, during survey planning, questionnaire design, sampling, training, fieldwork, data processing, data analysis, dissemination and archiving, ensuring that MICS protocols and recommendations are followed at all times. The consultant will communicate effectively between the UNICEF CO and NSC, participate in required meetings, and coordinate the work of other resource people hired by UNICEF to provide technical assistance. The Consultant will work in close collaboration with the Regional MICS Coordinators at UNICEF Regional Office and the MICS Team at UNICEF Headquarters, as well as expert consultants assigned to support the Uzbekistan MICS (collectively labelled "The UNICEF MICS Team"). Excellent oral and written communications in Uzbek, Russian and English required, knowledge of Karakalpak is an asset. The UNICEF family is committed to include everyone, irrespective of their race/ethnicity, disability, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, nationality, socio-economic background, minority, or any other status. UNICEF encourages applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of gender, nationality, religious or ethnic backgrounds, and from people with disabilities, including neurodivergence.
